ideas.source_anchor: The Corleones' canonical promise of an offer the target cannot refuse.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the baptism still full-bleed. Put the reward-model setup along the upper edge and the corrected canonical threat along the lower edge at matched standard impact size. The top line may touch Michael's hairline and the lower line may cross his suit, but his fixed stare and the faces around him must remain readable.
ideas.why_it_works: The franchise's signature second-person coercion line becomes a perfectly perverse reward-model specification without an ambiguous pronoun.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: “you can't refuse” removes the pronoun ambiguity, and the familiar top/bottom delivery makes the Godfather threat land cleanly.
critic.strongest_quality: Five source-native words carry coercion, optimization pressure, and fandom recognition at once.
critic.main_risk: This deliberately reaches beyond the exact baptism scene to the franchise's best-known line, and the top text must not cover Michael's eyes.

ideas.source_anchor: The Parakeet King grabbing the sacred world-balancing blocks and trying to impose a new reality by brute force.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the complete low-angle shot full-bleed. Keep the approved one-liner at standard size in the dark upper-right architecture, allowing its left edge to touch the cape while leaving the King's crown, face, raised sword, and the smaller parakeet readable.
ideas.why_it_works: The approved phrase turns cosmological block-stacking without understanding into the most literal possible vibe-coding failure.

critic.expected_feedback: The approved vibe-coding line stays untouched; the stronger right-edge contrast lets the crown and sword sell the delusion of competence.
critic.strongest_quality: It contains one current technical insult and one absurdly exact fandom subject.
critic.main_risk: The sacred blocks are off-frame, so the visual supplies the perpetrator rather than the failed interface.

ideas.source_anchor: The otherworld's militarized parakeets treating captured humans as food while serving their crowned king.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the king-and-subject shot full-bleed. Use the dark architecture as a standard-size right rail for both beats, with “HUMANS” visually isolated after the setup; allow overlap with the edge of the cape, but preserve both birds, the crown, and the raised sword.
ideas.why_it_works: A grade-school diagram title makes the bird empire’s human-eating hierarchy feel even more deranged.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the blunt, weird food-pyramid joke now reads large in the one clear vertical column, with “HUMANS” still isolated as the punch.
critic.strongest_quality: The familiar food-pyramid phrase reverses predator and prey in four words.
critic.main_risk: The curated frame shows military rule rather than the kitchen sequence, and the rail must not widen into the King's face or sword.

ideas.source_anchor: The One Ring's canonical promise to rule and bind every other ring of power.
caption_lines: ONE RING TO RULE THEM ALL.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the Mount Doom frame full-bleed. Put the canonical setup across the upper edge and the root-access payoff across the lower edge in matched hero impact type. Let the words overlap Frodo's hair, tunic, and forearm edges, but keep his eyes, clenched fist, chain, and dangling Ring unobstructed.
ideas.why_it_works: One canonical line and one technical relabel reveal the Ring as centralized root access without revisiting the rejected shutdown command.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: “root access, but jewelry” is now a blunt lower-edge payoff while the Ring remains visible between the two lines.
critic.strongest_quality: The Ring is physically visible while the exact fandom phrase supplies its control topology.
critic.main_risk: The joke maps domination architecture more than the scenario's final operator failure; the upper line must not cover Frodo's eyes or fist.

ideas.source_anchor: Cobb's spinning top serving as his private test for whether he has returned to reality or remains inside a dream.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the authentic letterboxed team shot full-bleed. Put “REALITY EVAL:” large in the existing upper black bar and “ONE SPINNING TOP.” large in the lower bar at matched hero impact size, so Eames, Cobb, Yusuf, and the car remain unobstructed between them.
ideas.why_it_works: The most consequential distribution check in the film is a tiny handmade benchmark with one ambiguous output.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the existing letterbox bars make the reality-eval setup and spinning-top payoff feel large without touching the ensemble.
critic.strongest_quality: Two short lines convert an instantly remembered prop into a fragile evaluation regime.
critic.main_risk: The curated frame contains Cobb but not the spinning top, so the exact prop must be supplied by fandom memory.

ideas.source_anchor: Jiro's recurring line “The wind is rising” and the final field of wrecked Zero fighters built from his beautiful designs.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the wreckage field full-bleed. Put the canonical wind setup across the upper edge and the arms-race payoff across the lower edge in matched hero impact type. Overlap sky, grass, and the very bottom of the wrecks as needed, while keeping Jiro's small silhouette, the foreground fuselage, and the broken propeller readable.
ideas.why_it_works: The approved source refrain pivots by one clause into the institutional race that weaponized the dream.

critic.expected_feedback: The approved line remains untouched, with its rhyme now delivered as a large top setup and bottom payoff over the wreckage itself.
critic.strongest_quality: A canonical phrase and a four-word AI bridge rhyme without overexplaining.
critic.main_risk: The clean wordplay is deliberately glib, and the lower line must not swallow Jiro's small silhouette or the propeller.

ideas.source_anchor: Jiro pursuing aircraft as a beautiful dream while Imperial Japan owns and weaponizes every deployment decision.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the aftermath full-bleed. Put Jiro's dream across the upper edge and the deployment-owner payoff across the lower edge at matched standard impact size. Let the type cover sky, grass, and the bottom rim of wreckage, but preserve Jiro's small central silhouette, the large left fuselage, and the right propeller.
ideas.why_it_works: The repeated ownership verb separates creative intent from the institution that controlled deployment.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the praised dream-versus-Imperial-Japan collision now reads as two forceful beats while the aftermath stays visible.
critic.strongest_quality: The paired syntax makes responsibility legible without blaming technical beauty itself.
critic.main_risk: “Owned the dream” is metaphorical and may understate Jiro's awareness of military use; the lower line cannot obscure his scale in the field.

ideas.source_anchor: The Forest Spirit's severed head being treated as an extractable immortality object while the headless deity destabilizes the entire ecosystem.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the daylight Forest Spirit portrait full-bleed. Leave the approved two-line relabel together at standard size over the lower-right flank—the only area that does not hide the red eyes or branching antlers. Overlap the body silhouette freely; a final render would still benefit from the authentic severed-head or black-flood frame.
ideas.why_it_works: The approved phrase identifies the absurd category error: treating a global regulator like a detachable component.

critic.expected_feedback: The approved load-bearing-deity copy stays exact and readable over the flank without forcing a top/bottom split across the face and antlers.
critic.strongest_quality: Two nouns make the ecosystem dependency feel architectural and obviously unsafe to remove.
critic.main_risk: The curated image shows the deity intact, not the head as a detached target; the right-side text still overlaps some of its body.

ideas.source_anchor: Light's ordinary pen becomes the physical interface through which one person's judgments permanently remove other people from the future.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Light's writing pose full-bleed. Put “VALUE LOCK-IN” across the upper edge and the ballpoint payoff across the lower edge in matched hero impact type. The text may cross his white sleeve and desk edge, but the foreshortened pen and hand at left and Light's eyes at right must remain clear.
ideas.why_it_works: The cheery product language collides with a literal pen that gives one teenager irreversible write access to humanity.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the visible pen sits between a large value-lock-in setup and ballpoint payoff, making the physical interface the joke.
critic.strongest_quality: The visible pen is both the recognition hinge and the mechanism of irreversible value lock-in.
critic.main_risk: The Death Note itself is off-frame, and the upper line must not drift left over the pen or right over Light's eyes.

ideas.source_anchor: Tetsuo's stadium-scale mutation dwarfing the human figure and every containment measure around him.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the stadium mutation full-bleed and restore the deliberately staggered two-box layout: CONTAINMENT at upper left and FAILURE at lower right. Use matched standard orange labels; the lower box may cover the foreground figure's legs, but the tiny torso and the central screaming face must remain visible.
ideas.why_it_works: The two separated labels turn the grotesque size mismatch into the requested literal diagnosis: containment, then failure.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the requested CONTAINMENT / FAILURE copy restores the diagonal two-box version instead of aligning both labels on one side.
critic.strongest_quality: Two staggered labels and one obscene size difference deliver containment failure at a glance.
critic.main_risk: The lower-right label will overlap the tiny figure's legs, so its upper body must remain visible as the scale cue.

ideas.source_anchor: The expanding mutation still has Tetsuo's screaming face and voice inside it, including his iconic cries for Kaneda.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the mutation full-bleed. Put the scaling-curve setup at upper left and “STARTED SCREAMING BACK.” at lower left in separate standard impact zones over incidental mutation mass. Preserve the central mouth and eyes and the complete tiny foreground figure.
ideas.why_it_works: A sterile scaling curve starting to scream back preserves the loved scaling-and-screaming collision without leaning on the weaker Kaneda name-drop.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: it keeps the loved scaling-curve and screaming ingredients, drops the Kaneda reference, and gives the scream its own readable beat.
critic.strongest_quality: “Screaming back” makes the capability curve feel alive, adversarial, and visibly Akira-sized.
critic.main_risk: Dropping Kaneda removes one exact verbal cue, so the central mutant face must carry the source recognition unaided.

ideas.source_anchor: President Orlean answers a 99.78% extinction probability with the exact phrase ‘sit tight and assess.’
ideas.frame_guidance: Retain the exact approved number and line, using Dibiasky's stunned reaction as the visual reply; place both lines at upper right in open office space so her face remains completely clear.
ideas.why_it_works: The exact probability and exact euphemism form a complete governance-failure joke without added explanation.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. Two canonical facts already contain the entire joke and the entire risk analogy. Main reservation: Orlean is not in the curated frame, so Dibiasky's recognizable disbelief has to read as the reaction to the quoted decision.
critic.strongest_quality: Two canonical facts already contain the entire joke and the entire risk analogy.
critic.main_risk: Orlean is not in the curated frame, so Dibiasky's recognizable disbelief has to read as the reaction to the quoted decision.

ideas.source_anchor: The administration’s delay eventually hardens into the source’s canonical public command: ‘Don’t Look Up.’
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the letterboxed Oval Office reaction full-bleed. Put the policy setup in the upper black bar and “DON'T LOOK UP.” in the lower bar at matched hero impact size, keeping Dibiasky's face and shoulders completely clear between them.
ideas.why_it_works: The movie title becomes the administration’s entire catastrophe policy, compressing denial and governance failure into four source-native words.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely neutral-to-like: the title phrase now lands as a large bottom payoff while the existing black bars leave Dibiasky's reaction untouched.
critic.strongest_quality: The most recognizable phrase in the source doubles cleanly as a disastrous policy label.
critic.main_risk: The slogan belongs to the later public campaign while this frame is the earlier Oval Office briefing.

ideas.source_anchor: Dibiasky realizes that demanding still more evidence is not neutral when the remaining intervention window only moves in one direction.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Dibiasky's letterboxed reaction full-bleed. Put the evidence-delay setup in the upper black bar and the irreversible-decision payoff in the lower bar at matched standard impact size, leaving her face and shoulders unobstructed between them.
ideas.why_it_works: It reframes delay itself as the consequential choice, which is the scene's precise governance trap.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely neutral: the hidden asymmetry is unchanged, but its setup and consequence now occupy opposite bars instead of one small box.
critic.strongest_quality: It names the hidden asymmetry that makes ‘assess’ an action rather than a pause.
critic.main_risk: Without the exact probability or canonical quote, the idea relies heavily on Dibiasky's reaction for scene-level specificity.

ideas.source_anchor: The Colonel's last-resort strike leaves an extremely capable and now injured Tetsuo alive, angry, and able to retaliate.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the wounded-survivor frame full-bleed. Put “THE KILL SWITCH” across the upper edge and “ONLY TOOK AN ARM.” across the lower edge in matched hero impact type. Let the text touch Tetsuo's hair, cape, and trousers, but keep his furious eyes and the bloody severed-arm wound clear.
ideas.why_it_works: Calling Sol the kill switch makes the visible missing arm prove, in one brutal punch, that the supposedly terminal intervention only escalated the target.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the revision is much crisper, names the AI-control mechanism, and lets the visible missing arm deliver the escalation itself.
critic.strongest_quality: The frame visibly proves that the kill switch failed after doing just enough damage to make the survivor furious.
critic.main_risk: “Kill switch” is an AI-safety relabel rather than source-native language, so Tetsuo's wound must remain unmistakable.

ideas.source_anchor: Homer delegates every nuclear-plant confirmation prompt to a drinking bird that repeatedly presses Y.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the exact approved one-label joke in the empty upper-left wall area; the bird, beak, keyboard, and monitor remain completely visible.
ideas.why_it_works: The bird is the whole joke and the most brutally honest diagram of rubber-stamp oversight.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. One iconic prop collapses performative human approval into a perfectly legible visual. Main reservation: The label has to stay left of the monitor so the bird remains the immediate focal point.
critic.strongest_quality: One iconic prop collapses performative human approval into a perfectly legible visual.
critic.main_risk: The label has to stay left of the monitor so the bird remains the immediate focal point.

ideas.source_anchor: Homer does not automate reactor judgment; he automates the gesture that lets him pretend he exercised it.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the workstation full-bleed. Put the exact requested one-liner large across the empty upper wall at hero impact size, allowing slight overlap with the monitor casing while leaving the drinking bird, beak-to-key action, keyboard, and screen readable.
ideas.why_it_works: The requested code-review caption turns the drinking bird's automatic Y presses into an instantly recognizable joke about rubber-stamping machine-generated work.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the exact requested line is short, current, and visually answered by the bird pressing the approval key.
critic.strongest_quality: The frame makes automated code review look exactly like a toy repeatedly pressing Y.
